spatial_entity.notes: Ancient emporium identified by modern scholarship with Ras Hafun on the northern Somali coast. The identification is suitable for a port-level participation claim but does not define a surrounding territorial-practice polygon.

claim.date_text_original: mid-first century CE; Casson dates the Periplus c. 40–70 CE
claim.summary: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea identifies Opone as an emporium exporting enslaved people to Egypt in increasing numbers. This is strong port-level evidence of slave-trade network participation, but it does not establish the origins of the enslaved people, their acquisition mechanisms, or the prevalence of slavery in the surrounding territory.

external_participation.role_text: Documented export node for enslaved people carried to Egypt
external_participation.notes: Do not derive a territorial-practice P-level from this claim. The database already models external participation separately from territorial practice through migration 0011.

source.title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
source.author_or_institution: Anonymous merchant; Wilfred H. Schoff translation
source.independence_notes: Contemporary/near-contemporary merchant itinerary describing the western Indian Ocean trading system.
source.reliability_limitations: The surviving text is transmitted through later manuscripts and the itinerary records commodities and ports rather than the local institutions, origins, or legal statuses by which exported people became enslaved.

evidence.evidence_role: direct source-native attestation of slave export

source.title: Nomads Trading with Empires: Intercultural Trade in Ancient Somaliland in the First to Seventh Centuries CE
source.independence_notes: Independent archaeological fieldwork and synthesis for ancient Somaliland and western Indian Ocean exchange.
source.reliability_limitations: The article establishes the northern Somali coast as an active exchange zone and contextualizes the Periplus ports; it does not independently establish local slavery institutions or the origins of people exported from Opone.

version.version_label: American Journal of Archaeology 126.1 (2022), published online 17 December 2021

evidence.evidence_role: specialist archaeological context for the port network
evidence.locator: abstract and discussion of Periplus far-side ports

source.title: Periplus — Introduction
source.author_or_institution: Dimitris Plantzos; National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
source.independence_notes: University scholarly contextualization of the Periplus, its dating, manuscript transmission, geography and commodity lists.
source.reliability_limitations: A contextual digital resource rather than a dedicated study of slavery; used for dating and source criticism, not to establish prevalence.

geometry.notes: Ras Hafun is the accepted working identification in the reviewed scholarship, but a point geometry should be resolved and provenance-recorded separately before publication. No territorial polygon is appropriate for this port-level participation claim.
